brief.headline: Cut the laminate price from ₹385.00/KG to ₹250.00/KG — Silk Polypack proves it's possible, and the market asks ₹205–305/kg.

priceAsk.summary: Ask for ₹250.00/KG on laminates, down from today's ₹385.00/KG.
priceAsk.basis: Silk Polypack gives us laminates at ₹250.00/KG today. The open market asks ₹205–305/kg for pharma/ORS sachet laminate (typical ₹250/kg), which the market calls fair. We're paying ₹385.00/KG — a 54.0% gap above what's reasonable.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move payment from 60 days to 30 days after receipt.

brief.financialLeverage: UFLEX is huge — ₹16492.00 Cr in sales — so our ₹64788 spend is 0.00% of their business; we're invisible to them. They're growing fast (35.5% a year), hungry for volume. They owe a lot (1.25× their own cash, total ₹10152.31 Cr), which means they value fast payment. Their profit is thin — they keep 4.1% of every rupee — so they won't give much away on price unless we bring more volume or threaten to walk. Bundle future orders or play them off Silk Polypack and Huhtamaki to get traction.

evidence.point: We pay ₹385.00/KG; Silk Polypack charges ₹250.00/KG for the same laminate.
The open market asks ₹205–305/kg (typical ₹250/kg) for pharma/ORS sachet laminate — the market verdict is that top-of-band is fair.
UFLEX's sales are growing 35.5% a year — they want new orders.
They owe 1.25× their own cash and carry ₹10152.31 Cr in total debt — cash matters to them.
We're 0.00% of their ₹16492.00 Cr revenue — tiny customer, so bundle volume or bring in a competitor to get leverage.

alternates.name: Huhtamaki India Ltd
alternates.why: Listed converter already supplying FDC a little; does pharma laminate sachets at scale (₹2758.00 Cr revenue, health C 59/100) — a proven second source.

alternates.name: Constantia Parikh Packaging Pvt Ltd
alternates.why: Part of global Constantia; makes pharma blister and sachet laminates in India (₹222.04 Cr revenue, health D 31/100) — smaller but credible pharma specialist.

risks: We're 0.00% of their business — on our own we have no pull; bundle more SKUs, commit multi-year volume, or run a live RFQ with Silk Polypack and Huhtamaki to force their hand.
They keep only 4.1% profit on every rupee sold — a deep price cut eats into that quickly, so they'll push back hard unless we offer volume or faster payment in return.
They carry heavy debt (1.25x) — small supply-continuity risk if cash gets very tight, though at their ₹16492.00 Cr scale it's unlikely; still, line up Huhtamaki as backup before you squeeze too hard.
Moving to 30-day payment frees up ₹5325 for us, but only works as a negotiation chip if they really need the cash — test whether faster payment buys a discount (even 2–3% would be worth it).
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We're here because we're paying you ₹385 a kilo for laminates when Silk Polypack charges us ₹250 and the market asks ₹205–305 — help us understand the gap and let's find a number that works for both of us.
